title: Some Sand Dunes Boom at 105 Decibels, Loud Enough to Hear for Miles

scenes.text: Some sand dunes roar loud enough to hear six miles away.
When sand avalanches down a steep dune face, the whole dune starts to boom.
It can reach one hundred and five decibels, about as loud as a snow blower.
It hums at a low pitch, around a hundred cycles per second.
Marco Polo heard it in the thirteenth century and blamed evil desert spirits.
The desert isn't haunted. It's just sand sliding.

description:
Some sand dunes boom at up to 105 decibels, loud enough to hear up to six miles away.
The sound happens when dry sand avalanches down the dune.
Would you want to hear it live?
first_comment: Would you slide down a dune to make it sing?
